overview: Are you interested in History, and want to see how it shapes the international system today? Then our History and International Relations combined degree is ideal for you. If you want to not only understand contemporary global affairs, but also want to know the events which have shaped the world we live in, then we have the course for you. Why did wars occur and why do we still have wars today? How do we account for historical inequalities, and are their effects still being felt today? Can individuals change history, or do global events transcend any one person? Does the imperialism of the past echo in the world of today? Whether your interest is migration, war, diplomacy, slavery or many other areas, by studying for a BA (Hons) in History and International Relations you’ll be able to look through the lenses of both a historian and an international relations theorist. You will find that these are highly complementary views of the world, but each will give you a subtly different understanding.
course_content_intro: The course content is made up of a variety of subject area strands that can be studied across all three years of the programme. At every level, there are modules relating to each strand. After taking the compulsory modules in the first year, you can choose to study across a range of strands, or specialise in particular strands. Below is a list of the strands and you can find the current modules on our website: brunel.ac.uk/ba-hir History (compulsory elements): This strand focuses world history. There will be a chance to explore the social, cultural and political dimensions to the formation and interaction of nations as well as important human phenomena such as exploration, migration and war. There will also be a chance to focus on what historians do and how they do it. You will look at debate, fake debate (e.g. Holocaust denial), controversy and primary sources and, in so doing, build up the skills for your dissertation. History (elective elements): This strand builds on the strand above. You will be able to develop specialisms in the history of Africa and America or focus on diplomacy and war or study issues of race, gender and identity International Relations (compulsory elements): This strand equips you with tools to understand contemporary International Relations at every level. It will focus on war and peace and the ways in which we understand the international system. You will also you develop the tools for sustained research in International Relations. This will include research design on qualitative methods, such as interview techniques. International Relations (elective elements): This strand builds on the strand above. You will be able to develop expertise in war and peace, Africa, Europe, the US, terrorism and intelligence.
assessment_and_feedback: You’ll be assessed by a combination of coursework and time-limited assessments, but most of your time will be spent in private study and reading. In your final year you will produce a final dissertation on a subject of your choice under the guidance of a dissertation supervisor.
careers_and_future: Studying on the History degree programmes will provide you with key transferable employment skills based on a wide range of written and oral communication skills in addition to analytical and critical thinking skills. Our programmes are built with input from business professionals with the specific aim of helping you enter the workplace fully equipped and confident of your abilities. Graduates from our History programmes have gone onto careers in a variety of private and public sectors such as working in government, NGO's, law, teaching, banking and researchers to name just a few areas. Many also undertake further study in order to become specialists in a given field.

overview: Perhaps history has always been an interest for you or it’s something you’ve developed an interest in by studying it at school or college. Either way, everyone on the History BA at Brunel starts off on the same level playing field, without the need for a history qualification. History is about understanding what it means to be human. Studying and analysing it will take you back into the societies of the past to help you understand contemporary issues all the more. It’s also a subject that will help to demonstrate your intellectual acumen and understanding of world affairs, which will be an asset in so many fields of work. Your studies at Brunel will focus on the history of Britain, Europe and the wider world in the modern period, looking closely at life as it was lived then, observing differences, similarities, patterns and connections with the present day. Along the way, you will build a toolkit of transferable skills gained through evidence gathering, analysis, problem-solving, drafting and communications, which can be applied to a wide range of industries within the public and private sector. Opt for a placement year and you’ll be adding a year’s experience in a job role and industry sector that will help to show future employers where you might be a good fit for their organisation. Your placement doesn’t have to be related to history and you’ll get plenty of support from staff and resources in the University’s Student Professional Development (SPD) to help steer you in the right direction. The course has established links to world-renowned archives and libraries based in and close to London, including the Caird Library (National Maritime Museum),The National Archives and the Imperial War Museum, among others. Additionally, the original WWII operations bunker used by Sir Winston Churchill on the former RAF Uxbridge site is a walk away from campus where Brunel students regularly volunteer.
course_content_intro: Our History programme offers an expansive and flexible curriculum designed to help you uncover the forces that shaped our world. From your first year, you'll build a solid foundation through core modules before tailoring your degree to suit your specific interests. Whether you choose to maintain a broad historical perspective or specialise in a specific area, you'll develop deep expertise as you progress toward your final-year dissertation. Our areas of study include African history, British and European history, Historiography and sources, race and gender history, and the history of intelligence, war and conflict.
assessment_and_feedback: You’ll be assessed on what you learn by a combination of coursework and exams. In your final year you will produce a final dissertation on a history subject of your choice under the guidance of a dissertation supervisor.
careers_and_future: Studying on the History degree programmes will provide you with key transferable employment skills based on a wide range of written and oral communication skills in addition to analytical and critical thinking skills. Our programmes are built with input from business professionals with the specific aim of helping you enter the workplace fully equipped and confident of your abilities. Graduates from our BA History programme have gone onto careers in a variety of private and public sectors such as working in government, NGO's, law, teaching, banking and researchers to name just a few areas. Many also undertake further study in order to become specialists in a given field.

college: College of Engineering, Design and Physical Sciences
overview: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming industries worldwide, creating demand for specialists who can design, develop, and evaluate human-centred intelligent systems that are intuitive and meet real-world demands. This requires expertise in both the technical foundations of AI and the human-centred design principles of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). Brunel’s Human-AI Interaction MSc is a technically oriented course combining AI, interactive system development, and human-centred principles. You will gain skills and practical experience prototyping and evaluating AI-enabled interactive systems, as well as working with programming tools, intelligent technologies, user experience, and human-centred AI approaches, preparing graduates for careers in interdisciplinary roles in AI and intelligent system design and development. Familiarity with programming concepts or computational problem-solving is therefore recommended. What you will learn in our MSc Human-AI Interaction You will develop practical skills in designing, implementing, and evaluating intelligent interactive systems. Key areas include: Human-centred AI Intelligent interactive systems AI-enabled user experience design Prototyping and developing interactive AI systems User evaluation and experimental methods Ethics and governance Data visualisation Who this course is for This course is particularly suitable for applicants with a background in: Computer Science Artificial Intelligence Data Science Software Engineering Engineering Mathematics Human-Computer Interaction (technical focus is recommended) Applicants from design or non-technical disciplines should demonstrate technical readiness, such as prior programming experience, practical coursework, software-related projects, or relevant technical training or self-learning certifications. Technical experience and tools During this Master’s, students may work with: Programming environments (e.g. Python) AI tools Interactive system development platforms Data analysis and visualisation tools Prototyping and evaluation techniques Human-centred AI frameworks Why study at Brunel? This MSc course is delivered at Brunel University of London, a leading UK institution in AI and HCI. You will join a truly international and diverse community, which has recently been ranked joint first in the UK and sixth in the world for ‘International Outlook’ by the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025. You will be taught by globally recognised experts in the computer science field, with nine academics in the department ranked among the top 2% of scientists globally (Stanford and Elsevier rankings 2024). Our department is also ranked ninth in the UK, and within the top 101-150 worldwide by the prestigious Shanghai global ranking of academic subjects 2024. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Is this course technical? Yes. This course combines AI, interactive system development, and human-centred design. Students engage with intelligent systems, programming tools, and technical development environments to prototype and evaluate AI-enabled interactive systems. Familiarity with programming concepts is recommended to fully benefit from the course. 2. Is this course suitable for students from non-computing backgrounds? Applicants from interdisciplinary backgrounds or non-technical disciplines may be considered if they can demonstrate technical readiness, such as programming experience, technical project experience or relevant self-learning. 3. How is this course different from a traditional MSc in AI? This course focuses specifically on the interaction between humans and intelligent systems. While students develop technical skills in AI and system development, the programme emphasises designing AI systems that are usable, effective, and aligned with human needs. This prepares graduates for specialised roles at the intersection of AI development and human-centred AI design.
assessment_and_feedback: The assessment includes a balance of coursework and examination (as detailed in the individual module specifications). Assessments range from written reports/essays through to an exam, design portfolios, practical coursework and programming exercises, according to the demands of particular modules and topic areas. Additionally, class tests can be used to assess a range of knowledge, including a range of specific technical subjects.
careers_and_future: The MSc in Human-AI Interaction prepares graduates for careers in intelligent systems design and development. Typical roles can include: Human-centred AI specialist AI UX engineer AI interaction designer Intelligent systems developer AI product designer Emerging technology specialist Graduates can work across sectors including technology, healthcare, finance, automotive, and immersive technologies.

modules.description: The Human-AI Interaction module bridges the interdisciplinary fields of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). It aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles, tools, and methods of designing and evaluating AI systems that interact effectively with humans. The module provides an in-depth exploration of relevant theories, models and skills required to be able to select and apply appropriate methods for human-centred AI-focused projects to improve the user experience. This includes understanding the range of approaches and frameworks available for structuring the design of human-centred projects, and when and how to apply them to be beneficial to diverse user needs. The module also focuses on how to evolve human-centred designs using prototyping methods and software, an important part of which is learning about the various methods for evaluating designs to maximise the user experience. In addition, the module fosters core design, communication and professional skills essential for effective collaboration in modern multidisciplinary teams, while encouraging responsible innovation and ethical considerations.

overview: Studying human geography and anthropology at Brunel gives you the opportunity to do fully funded fieldwork placements anywhere in the world according to your anthropological interests. This course combines the expertise of our staff and research across two closely related disciplines to develop your knowledge and skills in both Human Geography and Anthropology. Human Geography explores the complex relationships between societies and environments that are at the centre of the most important challenges that face people around the world today. Anthropology offers a unique and powerful understanding of cultural and social diversity in the modern world. It considers issues which can lead to mind blowing revelations about how individuals and cultures experience life differently. In the first year you will have an introduction to the fundamentals of both subject areas, and in the second and third years you will choose from a wide range of modules, choosing half from each subject. Within Human Geography, modules focus particularly around themes of cities and urbanism; post colonialism, race and migration; and political ecology and environmental justice. Key themes in Anthropology are childhood, youth and education; development, war and humanitarianism; and global health. Both subject areas offer opportunities to learn about the world immersively through fully funded anthropological fieldwork, developing skills that will make you highly employable. All students do a residential geography field trip in the first year and can opt to do another in the second year. Together these two subjects compliment each other and provide you with graduate opportunities in local and national government, international organisations, NGOs, the media, research and education.
course_content_intro: Your programme is split up into three different types of modules: Compulsory module: one which all students registered for the award are required to take as part of their programme of study. Optional module: one which students choose from an ‘option range’. A core assessment is an assessment within a module which must be passed in order to progress and to be eligible for the final award.
assessment_and_feedback: You’ll be assessed by a combination of coursework and exams, but most of your time will be spent in private study and reading. In your final year, you will produce a final dissertation on a subject of your choice under the guidance of a dissertation supervisor.
careers_and_future: A Human Geography and Anthropology degree from Brunel is your passport to a wide range of career destinations. You will acquire knowledge and understanding that is highly relevant to current world challenges, as well as an array of skills that will set you apart from other graduates. Fieldwork, in particular, requires you to practice skills in real-world settings. Not only will you learn to plan, collect and analyse data, but you'll also become adept at working in an unfamiliar environment, taking account of relevant ethical and safety issues, interacting respectfully with people, and problem-solving as a group and individually. If you opt for the four-year degree you will undertake a placement, either in an employment situation or undertaking extended fieldwork (almost) anywhere in the world. You will be fully supported in preparing for the placement and building a stronger CV. In the third year, you can opt for the module ‘Leadership for Change’ in which you will work with other students and with a community organisation on a project that will further develop your employability skills. Our course prepares you for careers in different fields including the local and national government, the environmental sector, international development, leisure and tourism, media and communications, planning, research, and academia.

matching_text: Human Geography and Anthropology BSc (Hons) Studying human geography and anthropology at Brunel gives you the opportunity to do fully funded fieldwork placements anywhere in the world according to your anthropological interests. This course combines the expertise of our staff and research across two closely related disciplines to develop your knowledge and skills in both Human Geography and Anthropology. Human Geography explores the complex relationships between societies and environments that are at the centre of the most important challenges that face people around the world today. Anthropology offers a unique and powerful understanding of cultural and social diversity in the modern world. It considers issues which can lead to mind blowing revelations about how individuals and cultures experience life differently. In the first year you will have an introduction to the fundamentals of both subject areas, and in the second and third years you will choose from a wide range of modules, choosing half from each subject. Within Human Geography, modules focus particularly around themes of cities and urbanism; post colonialism, race and migration; and political ecology and environmental justice. Key themes in Anthropology are childhood, youth and education; development, war and humanitarianism; and global health. Both subject areas offer opportunities to learn about the world immersively through fully funded anthropological fieldwork, developing skills that will make you highly employable. All students do a residential geography field trip in the first year and can opt to do another in the second year. Together these two subjects compliment each other and provide you with graduate opportunities in local and national government, international organisations, NGOs, the media, research and education. Your programme is split up into three different types of modules: Compulsory module: one which all students registered for the award are required to take as part of their programme of study. Optional module: one which students choose from an ‘option range’. A core assessment is an assessment within a module which must be passed in order to progress and to be eligible for the final award. You’ll be assessed by a combination of coursework and exams, but most of your time will be spent in private study and reading. In your final year, you will produce a final dissertation on a subject of your choice under the guidance of a dissertation supervisor.

modules.module_title: GY3611 - Climate Justice in a Changing World
modules.description: The module introduces students to current political and academic debates on climate justice in a changing world. The students will explore the different dimensions of climate justice, including the ways in which climate impacts and responsibilities are geographically (in space) and intergenerationally (over time) unequally distributed, and how they are stratified along class, race, and gender-based lines. The students will learn to analyse climate policies from a justice perspective, including questions related to historical and geographical responsibilities and the distribution of the costs and burdens of the green transition. Moving beyond a narrow focus on distributional justice, the students will also explore procedural and epistemic dimensions of climate justice. They will gain an understanding of the emergence and development of climate justice movements, their political challenges, and the role these movements have played in bringing justice questions to the forefront of the climate agenda.

modules.module_title: GY3610 - Modern Slavery and Human Trafficking
modules.description: This module provides a ‘meta-critique’ of both the dominant and critical claims related to modern slavery and human trafficking. The module aims to introduce students to the historical debates on labour and migration that led to the current international laws on ‘human trafficking’ (and national laws on ‘modern slavery’ in the UK and Australia). Students will be able to critically analyse the geopolitics of several competing terminologies, such as ‘human trafficking’, ‘modern slavery’, ‘forced labour’, and ‘unfree labour’. They will be able to critically evaluate whether and how these terms help address labour exploitation and/or are selectively deployed to serve certain political ideologies. Not only will students develop critical lenses to analyse the dominant paradigm of ‘modern slavery’ and ‘human trafficking’, but they will also be able to critically interrogate the strengths, weaknesses, and biases of the critical literature. Overall, the module is designed to encourage students first to engage with critical perspectives and then to go beyond them to decolonise one of the most politically charged debates of the 21st century, enabling them to develop original ideas on how to address the exploitation, oppression, and rightlessness of all workers.

overview: 5th in London for Business Studies — National Student Survey 2025 The Human Resource Management BSc is one of the few HRM programmes in the UK to hold AACSB accreditation alongside professional recognition from the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development (CIPD). On graduation, you'll be entitled to CIPD Associate Membership (Assoc CIPD) - a professional credential that sets you apart from non-accredited HR graduates and signals to employers that you're workforce-ready from day one. The programme covers the full HRM lifecycle: recruitment and talent acquisition, performance management, employee relations, reward, learning and development, and employment law. You'll examine how organisations attract, motivate, and retain people across different sectors, cultures, and regulatory environments. Specialist modules in Year 2 - Employment Relations and Engagement and Diversity Management in Organizations - give you a deep grounding in the most current workplace challenges. In your final year, HR Services and Analytics equips you to apply data and AI to people management decisions. Distinctive Features CIPD accreditation - graduate with Associate CIPD membership, the professional standard HR employers look for. CIPD is the world's largest professional body for HR and people development, with over 160,000 members internationally. Real-world HR practice - learning is built around authentic business case studies, workplace scenarios, and applied projects that mirror the tasks HR professionals handle daily: grievance investigations, recruitment campaigns, reward benchmarking, diversity audits. Flexible final year - choose between a substantial independent research project or a tailored set of optional modules to match your career goals. Ethical, sustainable, and inclusive HR - a strong emphasis on diversity, fairness, responsible management, and the role HR plays in building better workplaces. Research-led teaching - content reflects current HR trends: employee wellbeing, people analytics, AI in HR, hybrid working, and global labour markets. AI skills - at least 50% of modules across Brunel Business School now incorporate AI. In HR specifically, you'll use AI tools for workforce analytics, recruitment data analysis, and evidence-based people decisions - guided by the School's traffic-light assessment framework. London campus - Brunel's single-site campus in Uxbridge gives you a self-contained university experience, with central London 45 minutes away by tube. Placement employers and graduate destinations are concentrated in London and the South East. Placements, Employability & Outcomes An optional placement year between Years 2 and 3 lets you gain professional experience, earn while you learn, and build your CV in a real HR environment. Human Resource Management students from Brunel Business School have secured HR and people-related placements at organisations including GSK (Human Resources Placement, £27,000), AWS (Recruiter Intern, £26,400), Matillion (People Operations, £21,000), and Vintage Wholesale Supply (Operations & HR, £24,000). Across all Brunel Business School programmes, an audit of four academic years (2022–2026) identified 160 placement students securing roles at 136 unique employers spanning every major sector - from global pharmaceutical and technology companies to financial services, consumer brands, and the public sector. Placement salaries across BBS range from approximately £12,000 to £31,000, with an overall average of £21,260. Many placement students receive permanent job offers from their employer before completing their degree. Brunel was the first UK university to introduce year-long placements. 87% of Brunel Business School graduates are in work or further study within 15 months (Graduate Outcomes 2024), and placement graduates earn approximately 10% more on average. Brunel graduate salaries sit 11% above the sector average.
assessment_and_feedback: Assessment on the Human Resource Management BSc is designed to mirror the tasks you'll perform as an HR professional. Rather than relying solely on traditional exams, the programme uses authentic, practice-led assessments that develop and test the capabilities employers value. HR policy briefs and case analyses - you'll produce the kind of reports HR professionals prepare daily: grievance investigation summaries, recruitment campaign proposals, diversity audit findings, and reward benchmarking analyses - applying employment law and HR theory to realistic workplace scenarios. Workforce data projects - working with real organisational datasets, you'll analyse turnover trends, interpret engagement survey results, and present evidence-based recommendations - the same skills used by HR analysts, people operations teams, and HR business partners. Presentations - individual and group presentations develop the communication and influencing skills essential for HR roles, where pitching a policy change or presenting workforce insights to senior leadership is a core responsibility. Final-year project - a substantial independent report (approximately 8,000 words) on an HR topic of your choice, demonstrating the research, analysis, and communication skills that employers and postgraduate admissions tutors look for. Examinations - in selected modules, testing your ability to synthesise knowledge and apply employment law and HR frameworks under time pressure - as you would when advising a manager on a live employee relations issue. The approximate balance is 50% coursework to 50% examination, varying by module choice. Year 1 does not contribute to your final degree classification, giving you space to experiment and develop your skills without pressure. Year 2 contributes one-third, and Year 3 contributes two-thirds.
careers_and_future: 87% of Brunel Business School graduates are in work or further study within 15 months of completing their degree (Graduate Outcomes 2024). Brunel graduate salaries sit 11% above the sector average. Human Resource Management graduates pursue careers across the full spectrum of people management and organisational development. HR-specific roles include HR Assistant, HR Officer, Recruitment Consultant, Talent Acquisition Specialist, Learning and Development Officer, Employee Relations Advisor, and HR Analyst. Broader business roles include Business Development Executive, Management Trainee, and Training and Development Consultant. Graduates work across corporate organisations in the private sector, public sector bodies including the NHS and government, non-profit organisations and NGOs, recruitment and consultancy firms, and international organisations. The programme's CIPD accreditation means graduates enter the workforce with Associate CIPD membership - a credential that gives a measurable advantage in the HR graduate jobs market. Brunel HRM graduates have secured roles including People & Talent Administrator at Smart Managed Solutions, Employment Advisor at Belina Consulting Ltd, Human Resource Coordinator at Beaches Turks and Caicos Resort Villages & Spa, Business Support Executive at London & Partners, and Graduate Management Trainee at Relay Direct. Across all Brunel Business School programmes, graduates have been recruited by Accenture, Amazon, Barclays, Bosch, British Airways, Capgemini, GSK, HSBC, Jaguar Land Rover, L'Oréal, Microsoft, PwC, Rolls-Royce, and Xerox. A number of graduates each year progress to postgraduate study, including MSc programmes in Human Resource Management, Organisational Psychology, or Corporate Finance, as well as MBA programmes at leading institutions. Recent further study destinations include MSc Corporate Finance at King's College London and MA Philosophy at Central European University.

college: Brunel Business School
overview: The Human Resource Management MSc at Brunel provides a critical understanding of people management and analytics, combining theoretical knowledge with applied, practice-led learning. The programme is accredited by the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development (CIPD), the professional body for HR and people development, and its content is aligned with CIPD professional standards. You will study strategic HR leadership through a curriculum that integrates case studies from real organisations, live projects, and engagement with HR practitioners. The programme addresses contemporary workplace issues including AI and digital transformation in people management, diversity and inclusion, employee wellbeing, and global workforce challenges. You will learn to use HR data and analytics to support evidence-based decision-making on recruitment, retention, performance, and engagement. The programme offers a professional placement pathway of up to two years, enabling you to gain paid work experience in a UK organisation. You also have the option of a six- to twelve-week internship. Throughout your studies, you will benefit from guest lectures by HR professionals, industry visits, and enrichment activities - including psychometric testing, assessment centre experience, and the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator and Belbin team-role assessments through the Business Life Employability Programme - connecting your academic learning to professional practice. The programme is available with both September and January entry points. Study options include one year full-time, 16 months full-time with placement, or two years full-time with placement.
course_content_intro: The course consists of both compulsory modules which provide a strong basis of knowledge in HR and optional modules, which allow you to diversify somewhat in areas such as entrepreneurship and diversity in the workplace. What You'll Learn Strategic HR leadership and the employment cycle You will examine the full employment cycle - from workforce planning, recruitment, and selection through to performance management, reward, and retention. You will learn how to attract and assess candidates, design performance frameworks that align individual goals with organisational objectives, and manage employee relations. The programme also addresses how HR strategy connects to wider business strategy, enabling you to contribute to decisions at senior organisational levels. People analytics, AI and digital HR You will develop the ability to analyse employee data - including turnover, productivity, and engagement metrics - and to use HR metrics to inform decision-making. The programme examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping recruitment, employee monitoring, and workforce planning, and you will learn to evaluate both the opportunities and the ethical implications of AI in people management. You will also gain familiarity with digital HR tools and platforms used in contemporary organisations. Managing people across cultures and contexts You will explore how HR practices vary across national and cultural contexts, and how organisations manage people in international and comparative settings. This includes understanding cross-cultural leadership, global mobility, and the design of HR policies that are effective across different regulatory and cultural environments. You will also examine diversity, equity, and inclusion - learning to identify and reduce bias in recruitment and promotion, manage diverse teams, and create fair and inclusive workplace cultures. Employee wellbeing, development and organisational behaviour You will study how organisations support employee wellbeing, mental health, and work-life balance, and how to design learning and development programmes that build workforce capability. The programme also covers organisational behaviour - including leadership, motivation, team dynamics, and managing change - equipping you to diagnose and address workplace challenges such as low morale, resistance to change, and conflict. Skills You'll Develop Data and analytics skills You will learn to collect and analyse employee data - including turnover, performance, and engagement metrics - and to interpret quantitative and qualitative evidence to support HR decisions. This includes using HR metrics and analytics platforms to diagnose workforce issues and evaluate the impact of people management interventions. Digital and AI skills You will develop an understanding of how artificial intelligence is used in recruitment, performance monitoring, and workforce planning, and how to evaluate the ethical implications of these technologies. You will also gain practical familiarity with digital HR tools and platforms. People management and leadership skills You will build the ability to recruit and select effectively, manage performance through goal-setting and feedback, handle workplace conflict, and lead teams. The programme develops your capacity to design fair and effective HR policies and to manage people across diverse organisational contexts. Communication and influencing skills Through presentations, professional reports, and business cases, you will learn to communicate HR ideas clearly to managers and stakeholders and to influence decision-making at different organisational levels. Regular group work develops your collaboration and teamwork capabilities in multicultural settings. Strategic and critical thinking You will learn to link people management decisions to organisational performance, think long-term about workforce planning, and evaluate HR strategies and policies critically. The programme equips you to diagnose workplace challenges - such as low morale or high turnover - and to develop evidence-based, practical solutions.
assessment_and_feedback: Assessment on the MSc Human Resource Management is designed to reflect the tasks you will perform as an HR professional: Professional reports - You will analyse workforce data, evaluate HR policies, and produce evidence-based recommendations, mirroring the reports prepared by HR practitioners for senior management and board-level audiences. Strategic essays and case analyses - You will apply HR frameworks to real-world scenarios, evaluate comparative HR practices across national contexts, and propose strategic responses to organisational challenges. Research proposal - you will design a rigorous research project with a clear methodology, preparing you for both your dissertation and professional roles that require data-driven HR analysis. Examination - You will synthesise knowledge and apply frameworks under time constraints, comparable to professional certification assessments and senior-level decision-making. Dissertation - An independent research project on an HR topic of your choice, supervised by an academic expert. This mirrors the end-to-end research and evaluation projects undertaken in HR consultancy, policy, and strategic workforce planning.
careers_and_future: The programme is accredited by the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development (CIPD), providing you with access to professional development resources, networking opportunities, and the CIPD knowledge hub throughout your studies and beyond graduation. CIPD membership signals to employers that you meet the professional standards expected of HR practitioners. Career paths Graduates of the MSc Human Resource Management progress into a wide range of HR and people management roles across all sectors. Typical pathways include: General HR roles: HR Assistant, HR Coordinator, People Advisor. Progression: HR Manager, HR Business Partner, Head of HR. Talent acquisition and development roles: Recruitment Coordinator, Learning and Development Assistant, Talent Advisor. Progression: Talent Acquisition Manager, L&D Manager, Head of Talent. HR analytics and technology roles: HR Data Analyst, HRIS Coordinator, People Analytics Assistant. Progression: HR Analytics Manager, HR Technology Lead, Director of People Analytics. Diversity, equity and inclusion roles: DEI Coordinator, Inclusion Advisor, Equality Officer. Progression: DEI Manager, Head of Inclusion, Chief Diversity Officer. Employee relations and wellbeing roles: ER Advisor, Wellbeing Coordinator, HR Policy Officer. Progression: ER Manager, Head of Wellbeing, Director of People and Culture. HR consultancy and international HR roles: HR Consultant, Global Mobility Coordinator, International HR Assistant. Progression: Senior HR Consultant, International HR Manager, Global Head of HR. Placement outcomes Over the last three placement cycles (2023-26), 21 students from the MSc Human Resource Management completed professional placements with 20 different organisations, spanning healthcare, professional services, technology, education, and the non-profit sector. Among those placements where salary data was recorded, annual salaries ranged up to 22,880 GBP. Placement employers include PwC France (HR and Payroll Consultant), Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (Patient Access Coordinator), E3G (HR Intern), Career Teachers (SEN Teaching Assistant), CECOS College London (Student Placement Officer, 22,800 GBP; Admission and Attendance Monitoring Officer, 22,880 GBP), Cedar Brook Practice NHS (HR and Administration Assistant), Oxgate Gardens Surgery NHS England (Administration and Reception), CK Foods (HR Administrator), Prime Tuition (Human Resource Assistant), RJM Insulation (HR and Administrative Assistant), Future Connect Training and Recruitment, The Gurkha Centre, and iTech Services. Several employers recruited HRM placement students across multiple cycles, reflecting sustained demand: CECOS College London, Irecruit Now, and multiple NHS trusts including Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust and Cedar Brook Practice.

overview: The Guardian University Guide 2024 ranks Brunel design graduates top in the UK for career after 15 months, while government figures also show Brunel design graduates rank no.1 for graduate earnings in the UK.* Get a visual overview of this exciting programme by watching our colourful short video. Design at Brunel is all about realising fantastic ideas in the real world. Our Industrial Design BA/MDes Degree suits creative and practical thinkers who prefer to learn through building and evaluating project-based challenges, with a technological understanding and less theory and quantitative analysis. There is a lot of project-based learning to test your skills on all aspects of the design process, from contextual design ideas to realising your concept in the form of a product prototype. This means you’ll be able to build a great portfolio of your best-quality projects, academic and industry briefs, and case studies, during your studies. You’ll have workshop training and will use industry-standard equipment and software to develop quality hands-on skills to become a maker. You'll have access to modern facilities that include dedicated design studios, digital sketching, extensive prototyping workshops, as well as electronics and digital fabrication labs. The practical knowledge you gain is transferable to industry and provides a head start for your future career as a creative designer and design communicator in the modern world. This course can be studied 3 years full-time or 4 years full-time with placement starting in September. The placement year helps you to prepare for the world of work and you’ll have a year’s worth of invaluable professional experience when you graduate. Our students have worked in both small innovation start-ups and multinational organisations such as Chanel, Dior, Disney, Dyson and Lego. Our students have the opportunity to study abroad. You could spend a term or a year in one of our partner universities via our exchange programme: Politecnico di Milano in Italy; Delft University of Technology in The Netherlands, San Francisco State University in the USA and Institut Superieur de Design, ISD Bubika in France. New exchange opportunities are being developed with India, Canada and China. Made in Brunel is a unique, student-led initiative that showcases our design talent at its finest. Each year our students run a series of industry and community events leading up to the Made in Brunel exhibition. This annual showcase is a highlight of the London design calendar and promotes the incredible work our students produce to the creative community, and is a great way for our students to network with key design professionals. If you are interested in turning a product or technology idea into a business after you graduate, we are in partnership with the Central Research Laboratory (CRL) , a design incubator for start-ups. You’ll have access to meeting rooms and workspace as well as prototyping facilities. A team of in-house professionals will guide and support you at each stage and a number of our previous entrepreneurial students have successfully commercialised their products. The BA Industrial Design programme is fully accredited and recognised by the Institution of Engineering Designers (IED), the premier professional body representing engineering and product designers. * Longitudinal Employment Outcomes (LEO) 2022
course_content_intro: You’ll gain a sound grounding in technical and creative subjects before you move on to more specialised areas with a strong technological and humanistic focus. In your final year, you’ll learn advanced design innovation. Your major project is likely to include an aesthetic model and a functional prototype. The MDes year features further specialisation and research-led design.
assessment_and_feedback: Your progress will be assessed via assignments, coursework, presentations, individual and group design projects, lab reports and case studies, exams, and the final year major design project. Marked work and feedback will be returned to students within three weeks of submission.
careers_and_future: To help you prepare for the world of work, we’ll encourage you to take the placement option, incorporating a year spent in industry. This means you’ll have a year’s worth of invaluable professional experience and networks when you graduate. Our students have worked on placement for both small innovation start-ups and multinational organisations. Our graduate designers are highly valued in the industry, working around the world for organisations where excellence in design is crucial to the brand, including Apple, Audi, British Airways, Dyson, Habitat International, Lego, Microsoft, Philips, Procter & Gamble, and Virgin Atlantic.

college: College of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences
overview: Explore microbial pathogenesis, vaccines, and antimicrobial resistance on Brunel’s Infection and Antimicrobial Discovery MSc. You'll investigate the biology of microbial pathogens, the mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance, and the development of novel vaccines and treatments to combat infectious diseases. On this programme, you'll delve into microbial pathogenesis, host-pathogen interactions, and emerging infectious diseases. Topics include antibiotic mechanisms and resistance, bacterial biofilms, and novel vaccine strategies. You’ll also examine viral threats such as COVID and Ebola, and investigate cutting-edge approaches to antimicrobial discovery, including AI-driven drug design and alternatives to traditional antibiotics. You’ll be taught by internationally recognised researchers and gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge laboratories. The programme includes core training in molecular medicine, research methods, and scientific communication modules, alongside a course-specific module and an extensive research project. At Brunel, you’ll gain hands-on experience through research-led teaching, access to cutting-edge facilities, and valuable industry connections. Whether you're pursuing a future in biomedical research, clinical diagnostics, or the pharmaceutical sector, this degree will prepare you to make a real-world impact in science and medicine.
course_content_intro: On this course, you’ll acquire a comprehensive suite of scientific and professional skills. These include advanced laboratory techniques, data analysis, and bioinformatics, as well as the ability to critically evaluate scientific literature. You’ll also develop strong scientific writing and communication skills, enabling you to present complex information clearly to both specialist and non-specialist audiences. You’ll build strong independent research skills and develop a keen sense of ethical responsibility, setting you up for a wide range of scientific careers. Through specialist training, you’ll explore how pathogens interact with their hosts and investigate innovative strategies to combat antimicrobial resistance.
assessment_and_feedback: Your assessments are designed to reflect real-world scientific practice and help you build a broad and versatile skill set. Throughout the programme, you’ll be evaluated through a variety of coursework that mirrors the tasks of professional researchers. These include lab reports, data analysis, and even a grant proposal, giving you experience in the kinds of work you’ll encounter in research and industry. You’ll also develop your communication skills through written assignments, such as essays and articles tailored for both scientific and general audiences. An oral presentation will help you refine your public speaking and science communication abilities. To test your integrated knowledge, you’ll complete a synoptic exam, while a reflective seminar portfolio will encourage you to critically assess real-world scientific presentations and develop your analytical thinking. Your final challenge is the research dissertation - a substantial independent project where you’ll design, conduct, and communicate your own research, showcasing everything you’ve learned and your readiness for the next step in your scientific career.
careers_and_future: Graduates of Brunel's Infection and Antimicrobial Discovery MSc are highly sought after across a wide range of scientific and healthcare sectors. Whether you're aiming to work at the forefront of the fight against infectious diseases innovation or pursue further academic study, this programme opens the door to exciting and impactful career paths. Our graduates go on to thrive in careers such as: Infection-related Biomedical and Clinical Researcher Analytical Development Scientist Senior Scientist in Biotech Vaccine or Anti-microbial Clinical Trials Manager Science Communicator or Medical Writer Physician Associate or Healthcare Professional Previous Biomedical Sciences graduates have secured positions at leading organisations including Touchlight, MeiraGTx, and The Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, while others have progressed to PhD programmes at Brunel, UCL, and top international universities. Many have also taken on leadership roles in scientific communications and biotechnology firms. This degree also provides a strong foundation for further education and specialisation, including PhDs in immunology and infectious diseases, postgraduate certificates in clinical research, bioinformatics, or science communication and professional training in healthcare, data science, or regulatory affairs. Whether you’re looking to enter the lab, the clinic, or the boardroom, Brunel’s Infection and Antimicrobial Discovery MSc will prepare you to lead, innovate, and make a difference in the world of science and medicine.

overview: The MRes in Infection and Immunity is designed to provide advanced training in basic and translational research. Through a combination of two specialist taught modules and an extended independent research project (laboratory- or non-lab-based), you will develop the scientific, technical, and analytical skills needed for careers in research areas of immunology, related scientific fields, healthcare, and further doctoral study. This course is designed to provide you with research skills and an in-depth understanding of research methodology with specific relation to infection and immunity. You’ll build your scientific and technical expertise with the aim to investigate the mechanisms underlying infectious and immune-related diseases, and contribute to the development of novel diagnostics and therapies. Brunel’s MRes students receive the same support as PhD students. You’ll benefit from the expertise of our award-winning academic team of leading biomedical scientists specialising in infection and immunity research and receive support from specialist technical staff in a well-equipped research environment.
course_content_intro: The main focus of your MRes course is an extended independent research project. You will spend a substantial proportion of your time designing, planning, and conducting research in either laboratory-based or desk-based (i.e. bioinformatics-based) settings. Your project may explore areas aimed at understanding how immune responses can be enhanced and how disorders of immune dysfunction can be treated. This research contributes to the development of diagnostic biomarkers, vaccines against infectious diseases, and improved therapeutic strategies for infections, autoimmune diseases, and transplant rejection.
assessment_and_feedback: Assessment will take the form of written coursework, reports, grant proposal linked to topic of research project, portfolio of critical analyses and reflection on 5 seminars attended during the course, and MRes research thesis assessed by a viva.

matching_text: Infection and Immunity MRes The MRes in Infection and Immunity is designed to provide advanced training in basic and translational research. Through a combination of two specialist taught modules and an extended independent research project (laboratory- or non-lab-based), you will develop the scientific, technical, and analytical skills needed for careers in research areas of immunology, related scientific fields, healthcare, and further doctoral study. This course is designed to provide you with research skills and an in-depth understanding of research methodology with specific relation to infection and immunity. You’ll build your scientific and technical expertise with the aim to investigate the mechanisms underlying infectious and immune-related diseases, and contribute to the development of novel diagnostics and therapies. Brunel’s MRes students receive the same support as PhD students. You’ll benefit from the expertise of our award-winning academic team of leading biomedical scientists specialising in infection and immunity research and receive support from specialist technical staff in a well-equipped research environment. The main focus of your MRes course is an extended independent research project. You will spend a substantial proportion of your time designing, planning, and conducting research in either laboratory-based or desk-based (i.e. bioinformatics-based) settings. Your project may explore areas aimed at understanding how immune responses can be enhanced and how disorders of immune dysfunction can be treated. This research contributes to the development of diagnostic biomarkers, vaccines against infectious diseases, and improved therapeutic strategies for infections, autoimmune diseases, and transplant rejection. Assessment will take the form of written coursework, reports, grant proposal linked to topic of research project, portfolio of critical analyses and reflection on 5 seminars attended during the course, and MRes research thesis assessed by a viva.

overview: Get a visual overview of this exciting programme by watching our colourful short video. Our programme, one of the most comprehensive of its kind in the UK, will give you a solid grounding in the fundamentals of intellectual property and the opportunity to develop specialised skills through our wide range of elective modules covering both policy and practical technology-related issues. You can choose to study 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time (both start in September) or study 15 months full-time or 27 months part-time (both start in January). overview: The Brunel Intellectual Property Postgraduate Certificate (PGCert) is a unique, part-time programme with two separate routes designed for trainee patent attorneys with STEM degrees or for trainee trade mark attorneys. The PGCert is accredited with IPREG and provides two separate routes of Foundation Level Qualification (Patents) and a Foundation Level Qualification (Trademarks). Candidates may undertake either one or the other as part of the PgCert programme or combine the two FLQs in Patents and Trademarks as part of an LLM in Intellectual Property. In addition, Intellectual Property PgCert alumni have the option to upgrade to an LLM in Intellectual Property should they choose to re-enrol as returning students within the first five years after their graduation from Brunel. You will get a comprehensive overview of the theoretical, practical and management aspects of intellectual property at both national and international levels with a solid grounding in: Basic rules and principles of intellectual property law as well as the nature and scope of these rights Procedures for the granting and recognition of these rights Mechanisms for the enforcement of these rights Patents, copyrights, trademarks and contract resolution The course is suitable for law graduates and those with backgrounds in the sciences, technology, engineering and business. Non-graduates currently working in the area of intellectual property are also considered. No prior legal knowledge is required as you will be introduced to the essential legal principles throughout the course. As this is a part-time, you can remain in full-time employment while you study. UK employers currently sponsor over 80% of students taking the course. The programme runs from the end of September to the end of March and is delivered on Thursdays and will take 8 months to complete. overview: Intelligence and security policy issues are one of the fastest-growing areas of academic and public concern. More than ever before, national governments, international agencies, and international corporations need employees with a strong grasp of intelligence and security concerns who can also demonstrate first-rate skills of research and assessment. The intelligence analysis course at Brunel offers you a unique opportunity for practical, policy-oriented graduate study of intelligence issues across the private and public sectors around the world. The course is taught over nine months through a range of online resources, which include journals, e-books, specialised tools in intelligence analyst, and other materials such as government declassified documents. You'll connect to a team of supportive academic staff through online tutorials during their office hours and take part in a week-long residential course on campus consisting of workshops, presentations, and exercises. Highly committed and enthusiastic tutors combine broad-ranging expertise in areas such as cryptography, computer networking, imagery, intelligence analysis, economics and law, with the knowledge, skills and understanding to develop your academic and professional potential. You will be taught by some of the UK’s most innovative scholars in intelligence and security studies: an expert on covert action and military intelligence doctrine, a specialist in structured analytic techniques and a former senior military imagery analyst. These scholars are part of the Brunel Centre for Intelligence and Security Studies (BCISS) , which produces important original research that is published worldwide and contributes to the success of government and business in the UK. Graduates secure jobs in the private and public sectors, with most pursuing careers in intelligence and security studies. Those already in government employment find the course supports their promotion, commissions, or provides new employment opportunities post-retirement. Private sector opportunities are especially strong in analytical functions for the banking, resources, risk and security sectors.
course_content_intro: The Intelligence Analysis PgCert is structured around two compulsory modules.
assessment_and_feedback: This course is assessed via three types of assignments. Firstly, you'll complete a portfolio of short assignments to be submitted online, aiming to engage you with the key readings on a regular basis, gain frequent feedback from lecturers, and allowing you to interact with other students. The second stage of assessment will be during the residential week on-campus, where you will take part in presentations and exercises, giving you an opportunity to test the arguments you wish to make in your final essay as you discuss with your peers and academics. Finally, you'll submit a final essay where you reflect on your learning throughout the course.
careers_and_future: Within the UK, students with no service experience have gone on to work for the British Security Service, the Metropolitan Police Counter-Terrorism Centres, the Serious Organised Crime Agency, and other departments of government. Many students have noted to us that the innovative studies they undertook on our programme were important topics of discussion in their interviews. Those already in Government employment have successfully used their degrees to leverage promotion or commissioning. Students who have sought work in the private sector have likewise had success. Former BCISS students have gone to work for large banks conducting market analysis, to large oil-industry firms, to large consultancies, and to specialist private analysis firms such as MS Risk, Grey Dynamics, and many more. Indeed, MS Risk have had such success with our graduates that they have offered to fund a prize for the BCISS student who writes the best dissertation, annually. Overall, BCISS students have had a strong record of success in the years after their degrees.

overview: 2nd in London for Politics - National Student Survey 2025 Unlock the World of Intelligence with Brunel's Unique MA Programme Dive into the only MA in Intelligence that's designed not just to teach you about intelligence, but to prepare you for an impactful career in the field. At Brunel, our MA in Intelligence and Security Studies (MAISS) stands apart by offering a practical course grounded in both social science and historical methods. Why Choose MAISS? Flexible study modes: our course is offered in either “on-campus” and “distance learning” modes. The on-campus mode can be taken full or part-time. The distance learning mode is part-time, and includes one “residential week” each spring where the cohort will come to campus to complete their exercises and assessments together. These options allow you to study according to your requirements. Interdisciplinary Learning: Our programme uniquely blends social science, policy, and history to provide a rounded perspective on intelligence. Practical, Hands-On Training: Engage in immersive simulations, receive certification in industry tools, and participate in the Brunel Analytic Simulated Exercise (BASE) which provides real-world briefing experience before a panel of experts. Expert-Led Teaching: Learn from a dynamic mix of seasoned practitioners and renowned academics, ensuring your education is grounded in both theory and real-world application. Exclusive, Cohesive Curriculum: Experience a "garden-wall" designed programme where every module is crafted to build on each other. Offering a unique, cohesive learning journey, with specialist electives, focused on in-depth study. What Sets Us Apart? Our course is not just a history or politics degree. It's a policy-oriented programme that arms you with the practical skills sought by employers. Your learning and assessment are designed to provide you the tools and experiences you need to excel in the intelligence community, whether you’re on campus or distance learning. You will also be trained in Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) collection methods, for which you will receive a separate certificate. This is currently provided by Prevail Partners. Connect and Network Benefit from our extensive speaker series, bringing experts from government and the private sector right to your classroom. MAISS also boasts a vibrant community of peers and an expansive alumni network to build lasting professional connections. Our alumni are employed in the public sector, and private firms such as Securitas, Merck, Formula One, Pinkertons, Raytheon, and Lockheed Martin. Our graduates have also founded and joined smaller start-up intelligence companies such as Grey Dynamics and b4 Secure.

overview: On the International Arbitration LLM, you'll gain advanced knowledge in one of the most dynamic and globally relevant areas of legal practice. The programme is designed for law graduates and professionals who want specialist expertise, combining rigorous academic study with practical perspectives drawn from real arbitration practice. You'll explore international commercial arbitration, investment arbitration and alternative dispute resolution, while examining contemporary issues such as artificial intelligence in arbitration, cross‑border dispute resolution and the role of human rights in global arbitration systems. Through research‑led teaching, case analysis and practical problem‑solving, you'll develop high‑level analytical, advocacy, negotiation and legal research skills that prepares you to work confidently in international and multidisciplinary environments. A distinctive part of your experience is Brunel’s strong engagement with the legal profession. Because you’re studying in London - one of the world’s leading centres for international arbitration - you'll benefit from guest lectures and practitioner‑led sessions delivered by arbitrators, counsel and academics. It’s a chance to learn from experts, expand your network and stay close to current developments in global dispute resolution. You can also choose a placement option. This gives you the opportunity to apply your learning in a professional setting, typically at a law firm, and gain practical insight into how international arbitration and cross‑border disputes are managed day to day. Brunel Careers - Student Professional Development supports you in finding a placement, but placements aren’t guaranteed.
course_content_intro: You start by building a strong grounding in international commercial arbitration, investment arbitration and alternative dispute resolution. From there, you explore specialist areas that help you understand how arbitration operates across different legal, commercial and global contexts. Across your modules, you examine how arbitral tribunals work, how parties negotiate and present arguments, and how international rules and institutions shape cross‑border dispute settlement. You also look at emerging themes such as AI in arbitration, sustainability and ESG, international finance, and global regulatory frameworks. Throughout the programme, you apply your learning through case studies, research tasks and practical exercises that mirror real arbitration scenarios. You learn to analyse complex legal problems, construct persuasive arguments and communicate clearly with diverse stakeholders – skills that are valuable across the legal profession and beyond.
assessment_and_feedback: Students' progress is assessed through a combination of formative and summative assessments designed to develop both academic knowledge and professional skills. Depending on the module, summative assessments may include coursework essays, problem-based legal tasks, legal memoranda, presentations, group projects and examinations. Formative assessment and feedback are embedded throughout the programme to support students' learning and development before they complete assessed work. The programme culminates in a dissertation, enabling students to undertake independent research on a topic of their choice within the field of international arbitration.
careers_and_future: This LLM prepares you for careers in international arbitration and the wider field of cross‑border dispute resolution. You could work in arbitration or litigation teams at law firms, join arbitral institutions, or take on roles in in‑house legal teams within multinational businesses. Your skills also translate well to government departments, regulatory bodies and international organisations, where expertise in global dispute settlement is increasingly valued. If you’re interested in further study, the programme provides a strong foundation for doctoral research in arbitration, international law or related fields. You graduate with the confidence to work in international and multidisciplinary environments, and with the analytical, negotiation and communication skills that employers look for in arbitration practitioners and global legal professionals.

college: Brunel Business School
overview: Today’s international business managers and international entrepreneurs must be equipped with the necessary skills and capabilities to address the opportunities and challenges brought about by the digitalisation of world economies and geopolitical shifts. Our world increasingly requires forward-thinking, global talent in areas related to business leadership in an international environment. The MSc International Business and Entrepreneurship equips students with a comprehensive understanding of emerging issues and trends in a global context. Graduates will gain theoretical and professional grounding in the areas of international business and entrepreneurship, as well as technology management, innovation and sustainable development, and will develop analytical and personal skills needed in today’s globalised world. The MSc International Business and Entrepreneurship represents an excellent developmental opportunity for those who seek to pursue careers in new or existing organisations which operate across cultures and national borders. You will gain a comprehensive understanding regarding international entrepreneurial start-ups and global expansion in emerging and developed markets. You will be able to develop (and enhance) strategic thinking and key leadership skills necessary in the global environment such as decision-making and intercultural communication. Watch our video below to learn how the course will be taught, meet our academics and hear about the facilities available on our campus.
course_content_intro: The International Business and Entrepreneurship MSc programme includes a unique selection of modules which will give you a solid grounding in the areas of: international entrepreneurship, international business strategy, international management, international business ethics and corporate governance entrepreneurship, as well as small business management. You'll also have the opportunity to select two modules in the areas of: technology management, sustainable development policies and practices, entrepreneurial finance, international trade, as well as knowledge management, social networks and innovation.
assessment_and_feedback: Modules are usually assessed by individual assessment such as written essays, podcasts, posters or by examination in May. Coursework and examinations give you a chance to demonstrate critical and constructive thinking and reasoning. Your dissertation is a 12,000 word document that will show your ability to conceive, design and execute a major project, which confidently substantiates your chosen line of enquiry. Read our guide on how to avoid plagiarism in your assessments at Brunel.
careers_and_future: The new MSc International Business and Entrepreneurship provides students with a systematic understanding of emerging issues and trends in a global context. Graduates will gain theoretical and professional grounding in the areas of international business and entrepreneurship and will develop analytical and personal skills needed in today’s globalised world. It also provides the essential skill-sets to better accommodate today's global business environment and provide students with employment options in the long term. Graduates will gain the knowledge and skills suitable for a broad range of careers including positions in the management of multinational firms (export manager, international sales executive; business analyst; business development manager, international sales executive, etc.), in international consultancy firms, local and national governmental institutions as well as international NGOs. Graduates will also be able to develop or enhance entrepreneurial competencies for starting and operating their own international start-ups. Furthermore, this programme also enables students interested in to perusing an academic career to set a solid basis for engaging in a doctoral programme. Some of the well-known names who value Brunel Business School graduates include Accenture, Amazon, Barclays, British Airways, Capgemini, HSBC, Jaguar Land Rover, L’Oréal, McCann, Microsoft, PricewaterhouseCoopers and Xerox.

The research-led programme is designed to help you acquire advanced knowledge in the relationships between international business, environment and society, and how international business can address the overarching social and environmental problems of climate change and biodiversity loss effectively. Through a combination of theoretical and practical modules, you will develop business, forward-thinking, and analytical skills which are essential for success in driving business forward both sustainably and holistically. modules.description: The aim of this module is to enable students to understand sustainability from an environmental governance perspective for businesses. The module will help students develop a critical understanding about managing our natural resources. The business risks posed by climate change and biodiversity loss will be discussed. The mechanisms adopted by businesses to mitigate biodiversity loss will be critically analysed.

college: Brunel Business School
overview: 5th in London for Business Studies - National Student Survey 2025 The International Business BSc combines a rigorous business education - economics, strategy, marketing, finance - with specialist modules on global trade, emerging markets, and cross-border operations. The programme is one of the few in the UK to hold AACSB accreditation alongside professional recognition from the Institute of Export and International Trade (CIEIT), offering exemptions from professional examinations and access to industry networks before you graduate. The programme examines the forces reshaping international business: trade policy, supply chain disruption, the rise of emerging economies, and AI-driven transformation. In Year 2, you'll take a dedicated module on International Business in Emerging Markets, analysing how multinationals, indigenous firms, and host governments compete and collaborate. Core modules also cover international economics, global strategy, cross-border investment, and international human resource management - preparing you to make confident decisions in conditions of uncertainty. Distinctive Features Annual International Business Week - a dedicated programme of guest lectures, panel discussions, and networking sessions where policymakers, trade specialists, and multinational executives come to campus to discuss real-time issues: the impact of tariffs on supply chains, the role of AI in cross-border operations, and the geopolitics of trade. Thought Leadership Series - running throughout the year, featuring industry experts who explore the most pressing questions in international business. CIEIT accreditation - professional recognition providing a direct pathway into careers in international trade, logistics, and export management, plus access to exclusive training, networking, and resources. AI skills - at least 50% of modules across Brunel Business School now incorporate AI, preparing you to use artificial intelligence for market research, competitive analysis, and data-driven decisions, guided by the School's traffic-light assessment framework. Field visits - to London-based global organisations, supplementing classroom learning with first-hand exposure to international operations. Placements, Employability & Outcomes An optional placement year between Years 2 and 3 lets you gain professional experience and earn while you learn. International Business students have secured placements at AWS (£26,400), GSK (£27,000), Bosch (£22,500), UBS, Kantar Worldpanel (£22,700), Matillion (£21,000), The Stay Club (£24,420), and RWC (£20,000), with an average placement salary of approximately £20,750. Typical placement roles include Sales Operations Associate, Strategic Operations Assistant, Marketing Executive, and Retail Operations Management Intern. Brunel was the first UK university to introduce year-long placements. 87% of Brunel Business School graduates are in work or further study within 15 months (Graduate Outcomes 2024). Over the past four years, 160 Brunel Business School students have secured placements at more than 130 organisations. International Business graduates pursue careers in multinational corporations, trade and export organisations, consultancy firms, financial institutions, and public-sector bodies with international operations. Typical roles include international business development manager, global strategy analyst, trade and investment adviser, supply chain manager, and export manager. Employers of Brunel Business School graduates include Accenture, Amazon, Barclays, Bosch, British Airways, Capgemini, GSK, HSBC, Jaguar Land Rover, L'Oréal, Microsoft, PwC, Rolls-Royce, and Xerox.
course_content_intro: Compulsory modules in your first and second year will cover the fundamentals on conducting business in a global market. Optional modules in your final year twinned with your dissertation, will give you the opportunity to branch out and specialise in an area which particularly interests you.
assessment_and_feedback: Assessment on the International Business BSc is designed to mirror the tasks you'll perform in a professional international business career. Rather than relying solely on traditional exams, the programme uses authentic, practice-led assessments that develop and test the capabilities employers value. Strategy reports - you'll produce competitive analysis and market-entry recommendations of the kind expected by consultancy firms and corporate strategy teams, applying international business theory to real company and country contexts. Data analysis projects - working with real international trade datasets, you'll analyse market trends, interpret trade statistics, and present evidence-based recommendations - the same skills used by trade analysts, policy advisers, and business development teams. Presentations - individual and group presentations develop the cross-cultural communication and pitching skills essential for international client-facing roles. Final-year project - a substantial independent report (approximately 8,000 words) on an international business topic of your choice, demonstrating the research, analysis, and communication skills that employers and postgraduate admissions tutors look for. Examinations - in selected modules, testing your ability to synthesise knowledge and think under pressure, as you would in a boardroom or client briefing. The approximate balance is 50% coursework to 50% examination, varying by module choice. Year 1 does not contribute to your final degree classification, giving you space to experiment and develop your skills without pressure. Year 2 contributes one-third, and Year 3 contributes two-thirds.
careers_and_future: This degree is designed to equip you with the skills and experience needed to thrive in the global job market. You’ll benefit from extensive industry links as well as a strong network of employers, ensuring that you’re highly sought after by top organisations worldwide. All our business degrees offer an optional work placement year, giving you the opportunity to gain hands-on industry experience with leading global companies such as Accenture, Amazon, Barclays, British Airways, Capgemini, HSBC, Jaguar Land Rover, L’Oréal, McCann, Microsoft, PricewaterhouseCoopers, and Xerox. This experience is highly valued by employers and gives you a competitive edge when applying for graduate roles. Our careers programmes are developed in collaboration with business professionals to ensure you graduate workplace-ready. In addition, our Business Life programme offers tailored professional and personal development sessions, covering essential skills such as customer service, teamwork, presentation skills, and project management. At Brunel Business School, we’re committed to preparing you for a successful career in international business, trade, consultancy, and management. Our strong focus on employability, industry partnerships, and global exposure ensures that you’re well-prepared to make an impact in today’s rapidly evolving business world.
